newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-QNI to continue scout for nickel ore.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-QNI to continue scout for nickel ore.

text.p: Nickel producer QNI Ltd will evaluate further opportunities as they arise to secure future ore supplies for its Queensland-based refinery business, a company spokeswoman said on Thursday.
QNI earlier on Thurday said it had reached an agreement with New Caledonian miner, Noumea Enerprises SA to jointly explore nickel tenements in New Caledonia's southern province.
"It's a continuing programme, we're looking at all different areas," the spokeswoman said.
The agreement follows earlier alliances forged by QNI with other interests in New Caledonia and in South Africa and Indonesia to become more of an integrated nickel company.
"QNI has a strategy to secure and diversify long-term ore supplies and this agreement goes a long way towards serving that strategy," the spokeswoman said.
Under the most recent agreement, QNI would subscribe for 40 percent of the shares of Noumea for A$750,000, to be used for exploration funding to run through mid-1997, she said.

QNI, which will produce about 29,000 tonnes of nickel in 1996 from its works in July unveiled a three way agreement that could lead to an integrated processing business in Indonesia and Australia that would boost QNI's nickel and cobalt output.
The agreement was reached with South Africa's Gencor Ltd and P.T. Aneka Tambang of Indonesia to study such a plan.
QNI currently draws only about a third of its nickel ore from the Gebe Island deposit in Indonesia, mined by Aneka Tambang, with the rest coming from New Caledonia.

Earlier this month, QNI took a 67 percent stake in a joint venture with Societe des Mines de la Tontoua of New Caledonia to acquire 40 existing mine tenements in the northern province for A$35 million, paid over 15 years.
